## My Thinking

I have been farming this same land in Quzhou my whole life. My husband is gone, my son works in Baoding, so it is just me. I have 4 mu of flat, good soil — the kind this county is known for. I do not need to think much about what to grow. Everyone here does the same thing: wheat in the winter, maize in the summer. That is what this land does. That is what I know.

For wheat, I will go to the village supply shop and buy the same improved seed I used the past two years — the one the village promoted, a local Hebei variety. It did fine. I will not try something new at my age. I will hire the neighbor's rotary tiller before I sow, then put down compound fertilizer and urea as base dressing. At jointing stage I will top-dress with urea again. I water three times: once before winter sets in hard, once at jointing, once when the heads come out. I spray herbicide in early spring and one more time for aphids before harvest. The harvester comes in June and I sell most of what I get.

Then right after harvest, same land, I plant summer maize with hybrid seed — Zhengdan 958 or Xianyu 335, whatever the shop has. I broadcast fertilizer, direct-seed into the wheat stubble — no need to till twice, my body cannot take that. Summer rains usually help but I pump water twice to be safe. One herbicide spray early. The machine comes back in September.

I do not grow vegetables to sell. Just a small patch by the house for myself, that is not farming, that is just eating.
